papers.title: Operando Mapping of Population Phase Separation and Lithium‐Plating Dynamics in Graphite Electrode Using Optical Microscopy and Microstructure Modeling
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The fast‐charging capability of phase‐separating graphite electrodes is largely constrained by heterogeneous reaction kinetics and sluggish mass transport at both the particle and electrode scales, which increase the risk of parasitic lithium plating and associated safety concerns. A deeper mechanistic understanding of the interplay among phase‐separation dynamics, electrode microstructure, and lithium‐plating propensity is therefore essential for guiding the rational design of advanced electrode architectures and fast‐charging protocols. Here, we combine operando optical microscopy with three‐dimensional microstructure‐resolved phase‐field modeling to resolve the interplay between phase separation and lithium plating. Microscopy captures stages evolution, phase mode transitions and structural dynamics across the particle population and at the single‐particle level, which is driven by the slow interfacial reactions. Non‐equilibrium phase‐field simulations elucidate the kinetic control mechanisms governing phase transitions as the current varies. Importantly, a new mechanism of lithium plating associated with interfacial ohmic resistance is identified. Based on these insights, we evaluate particle‐size‐distribution design and use thermal activation as a mechanistic probe to resolve how temperature alters phase‐separation pathways and lithium‐plating behavior. These results may serve as a foundation for improving the physical understanding and driving optimization of fast charging protocols for lithium‐ion batteries.
papers.tldr: This study combines operando optical microscopy with 3D microstructure-resolved phase-field modeling to reveal how phase-separation dynamics and interfacial ohmic resistance drive lithium plating in graphite electrodes, informing particle-size and thermal design for faster-charging lithium-ion batteries.

papers.title: Engineering Li + Transport in Ni‐Rich Layered Cathodes Toward Homogenization
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Nickel‐rich layered oxide (NRLO) cathodes (Ni≥80%) are promising for next‐generation lithium‐ion batteries with energy densities exceeding 300 Wh kg −1 , but suffer from rapid degradation under deep delithiation, including phase transitions, microcracking, and surface reconstruction. These failure modes are increasingly recognized to be coupled through heterogeneous Li + transport across multiple length scales. Here we show that spatial variations in Li + transport originate from atomic, structural, and interfacial factors and ultimately evolve into macroscopic chemo‐mechanical degradation. On this basis, we introduce transport homogenization as a unifying design principle for regulating Li + transport in NRLO cathodes. Within this framework, diverse material engineering strategies, including bulk structural design, interfacial transport engineering, and dynamic transport regulation, are interpreted from a common transport‐centered perspective. We further summarize emerging characterization approaches for quantifying transport heterogeneity and discuss future opportunities for establishing predictive cross‐scale design principles. Overall, this review establishes a transport‐centered framework that unifies degradation in NRLO cathodes and provides a mechanistic basis for rational design of next‐generation high‐energy‐density cathode materials.
papers.tldr: This review proposes **transport homogenization** as a unifying design principle to regulate Li⁺ transport across atomic-to-macroscopic scales in Ni-rich layered cathodes, linking heterogeneous transport to chemo-mechanical degradation and guiding next-generation high-energy-density battery cathodes.

papers.title: Reaction-priority gating enables ionic-liquid electrolytes for 80°C lithium metal batteries
papers.abstract: High-temperature operation magnifies interfacial parasitic reactions in lithium metal batteries, rapidly depleting cyclable Li and destabilizing Ni-rich layered oxide cathodes. Here we introduce a reaction-priority gating strategy for ionic-liquid electrolytes...
papers.tldr: A reaction-priority gating strategy in ionic-liquid electrolytes suppresses interfacial parasitic reactions, stabilizing Ni-rich cathodes and cyclable Li to enable lithium metal batteries operating at 80°C.

papers.title: Diagnosing the Role of Mn Additives in Aqueous Zn/MnO 2 Batteries
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Manganese dioxides are pervasive as cathode materials for aqueous zinc‐ion batteries; however, their energy storage mechanism has proven to be complex. Increasing evidence suggests that Mn dissolution contributes to cathode capacity via a reversible dissolution‐redeposition process, in addition to capacity from Zn 2+ /H + (de)intercalation. Understanding the role played by Mn 2+ in the electrolyte, particularly when introduced as an electrolyte additive, is important for diagnosing cathode degradation. Using operando X‐ray fluorescence (XRF) spectroscopy, we track Mn 2+ in operating cells to gain insights into the complexity of the MnO 2 cathode. While some suppression of cathode dissolution by the additive cannot be excluded, our measurements suggest that Mn 2+ electrolyte additives improve cycling performance by supplying extra redox‐active Mn during charge, rather than solely by suppressing Mn dissolution, thereby compensating for cathode degradation. Benefiting from operando XRF, we propose that a potential contributor to capacity fading is the incomplete dissolution of the MnO 2 cathode and incomplete redeposition of Mn 2+ from the electrolyte, and that this fading does not appear to be mitigated by using Mn 2+ additives. These findings underscore the necessity of directly tracking Mn 2+ evolution, and that improving reversibility requires addressing both the dissolution of MnO 2 and the redeposition of Mn 2+ .
papers.tldr: Using operando X-ray fluorescence, this study shows that Mn²⁺ electrolyte additives improve aqueous Zn/MnO₂ battery cycling mainly by supplying redox-active Mn during charge rather than solely suppressing cathode dissolution, while capacity fading from incomplete MnO₂ dissolution and Mn²⁺ redeposition remains unmitigated.

papers.title: Fundamental Design Principles and Engineering Strategies of Liquid‐Phase Electrolytes for Highly Durable Rechargeable Lithium Metal Batteries
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium (Li) metal has emerged as the premier anode candidate in next‐generation high‐energy‐density batteries due to its ultrahigh theoretical capacity and ultralow electrochemical potential. However, critical technical barriers persist in Li metal anode implementation, such as uncontrolled Li dendrite growth and persistent interfacial side reactions. Acting as the mediating agent between cathodes and anodes, electrolytes critically determine battery overall performance. Taking solvent‐salt‐additive components as the entry point, adopting liquid‐phase electrolyte engineering strategies to optimize electrolyte composition and regulate solvation structure can not only address the inherent issues of Li metal anodes, but also endow Li metal batteries with desired performances, including high safety, high‐voltage tolerance, fast‐charging capability, and wide‐temperature operation. In this review, the design principles of reliable liquid‐phase electrolytes for Li metal batteries are discussed in detail. The essential liquid‐phase electrolyte engineering strategies, including designing new‐type salt/solvent molecular architectures, restructuring salt‐solvent combination systems, incorporating electrolyte additives with various functions, utilizing (localized) high‐concentration electrolytes, and developing brand‐new electrolyte formulations for adapting to different temperature ranges, are comprehensively summarized. Moreover, emerging design strategies, future design considerations, and remaining challenges in electrolyte engineering are highlighted, with the aim of pointing out potential opportunities to propel the practical development of Li metal batteries.
papers.tldr: This review outlines design principles and engineering strategies for liquid-phase electrolytes—including solvent/salt/additive design, high-concentration formulations, and solvation-structure regulation—to suppress dendrite growth and interfacial side reactions and enable durable, high-performance rechargeable lithium metal batteries.

papers.title: Constructing Hybrid Solid–Liquid Li+ Transport Networks for Fast-Charging Thick Electrodes
papers.abstract: Abstract Fast-charging technology for high-energy-density lithium-ion batteries remains constrained by high interfacial impedance and sluggish Li+ transport within electrodes. Herein, hierarchical-sized Li1.5Al0.5Ti1.5(PO4)3 (LATP, particle ranging from 5 to 500 nm) is used to construct a hybrid solid–liquid Li+ transport network in high-mass-loading cathodes (27 mg cm–2). A combination of different characterization techniques is employed to understand the underlying working principle of LATP from the particle to the electrode scale. LATP nanograins (∼10 nm) adsorbed onto cathode particle surfaces reduce Li+ desolvation energy (43.30 vs 52.97 kJ mol–1) and stabilize a thin CEI after cycling. Submicron LATP particles (320–480 nm) infiltrate pores of thick electrodes, forming interconnected networks that increase the Li+ diffusion coefficient. Furthermore, LATP increases the Li+ transference number of the liquid electrolyte within LATP-permeated regions. Consequently, LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2||Li cells with LATP-blended cathodes deliver dramatically enhanced rate performance (102 vs 36 mAh g–1 at 0.75C and –10 °C).
papers.tldr: Hierarchical LATP particles build a hybrid solid–liquid Li⁺ transport network in thick high-mass-loading cathodes, lowering desolvation energy and enhancing Li⁺ diffusion/transference to enable dramatically improved fast-charging performance.

papers.title: Capturing the Hidden Short-Range Order in Amorphous Oxide Interfaces That Directs Quasi-Epitaxial Thin-Film Growth
papers.abstract: Abstract As solid-state device architectures become increasingly complex, buried interfaces play a critical role in determining thin-film texture, morphology, and defect formation. However, resolving the structural features that control growth on nominally amorphous interlayers remains challenging because it requires three-dimensional sensitivity at high spatial resolution. Here, we combine four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy, fluctuation electron microscopy, and multislice electron ptychography to investigate ruthenium (Ru) thin films grown on an underlying amorphous Ta2O5 layer, a material stack relevant for next-generation electronic and spintronic devices. Although the Ta2O5 layer appears amorphous in conventional imaging, diffraction and depth-resolved ptychographic reconstructions reveal nanoscale β-Ta2O5-like ordered motifs near the Ru/Ta2O5 interface. These locally ordered motifs, together with the interfacial morphology, guide the orientation of the Ru layer and produce a textured, quasi-epitaxial film. The curved and atomically rough interface further induces depth-dependent strain gradients and promotes planar defect formation within the Ru layer. Collectively, these results demonstrate that hidden short-range order within nominally amorphous oxides can direct the growth of metallic thin films, providing a framework for engineering buried interfaces in advanced electronic and spintronic material stacks.
papers.tldr: Using 4D-STEM, fluctuation electron microscopy, and multislice ptychography, this study reveals that hidden nanoscale β-Ta2O5-like short-range order in a nominally amorphous Ta2O5 interlayer directs the quasi-epitaxial growth and strain/defect evolution of Ru thin films.

papers.title: Video-rate volumetric chemical imaging via mid-infrared photothermal optical diffraction tomography
papers.abstract: Abstract Label-free vibrational microscopy provides chemically specific access to cellular structures, yet quantitative volumetric imaging of intracellular dynamics remains challenging on subsecond timescales. Here, we demonstrate video-rate mid-infrared photothermal optical diffraction tomography (MIP-ODT) by combining high photothermal sensitivity with rapid angular scanning. The system achieves 19.2 volumes per second, nearly 400 times faster than previous MIP tomography implementations, with a signal-to-noise ratio exceeding 70 and no temporal averaging. We track lipid droplets in living cells and quantify anomalous diffusion from three-dimensional trajectories, revealing heterogeneous intracellular transport behaviors obscured in two-dimensional measurements. Rapid mid-infrared wavenumber sweeping further enables broadband multi-wavenumber volumetric chemical imaging across a 300 cm⁻¹ spectral window within 1 s. These results establish MIP-ODT as a platform for high-speed, label-free volumetric chemical imaging of single cells and quantitative investigation of dynamic intracellular organization.
papers.tldr: This paper presents video-rate mid-infrared photothermal optical diffraction tomography (MIP-ODT), enabling label-free, high-speed 3D chemical imaging of living cells and quantitative tracking of intracellular dynamics and broadband vibrational information.

papers.title: Chirality-selective second-harmonic response with Floquet engineering
papers.abstract: Symmetry breaking profoundly influences the macroscopic physical properties of materials. For instance, inversion symmetry breaking in monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides enables the emergence of chiral selection rules, featuring distinct optical chirality-selective electronic properties. Here, we demonstrate ultrafast, coherent manipulation of chirality-selective nonlinear optics in monolayer molybdenum disulfide (MoS 2 ) through time-reversal symmetry breaking via Floquet engineering. By using sub-bandgap, circularly polarized ultrafast optical pulses, we introduce nondegenerate, chirality-selective optical Stark and Bloch-Siegert shifts. This approach effectively lifts the energy degeneracy, leading to pronounced chirality-selective second-harmonic generation. Furthermore, we reveal that the Floquet-engineered chirality-selective states can be finely tuned using optical parameters such as intensity and chirality. Our results show a method for manipulating the energy degree of freedom, paving the way for ultrafast nonlinear photonics.
papers.tldr: Floquet engineering with circularly polarized sub-bandgap pulses breaks time-reversal symmetry in monolayer MoS₂, enabling ultrafast, tunable chirality-selective second-harmonic generation.

papers.title: Constructing an Adaptive Flexible Interphase on Halide Electrolytes by Lewis‐Acid‐Induced Polymerization for High‐Voltage All‐Solid‐State Lithium Batteries
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT All‐solid‐state lithium batteries (ASSLBs) combining halide solid electrolytes (HSEs) with high‐nickel layered oxide cathodes offer great promise for high energy density, yet they suffer from severe interfacial issues such as oxidative decomposition, mechanical degradation, and chemical incompatibility with sulfide electrolytes. Herein, we report a Lewis‐acid‐induced surface‐softening strategy that constructs a nanoscale adaptive flexible interphase (AFI) via in situ polymerization of acrylonitrile (AN) on a representative halide electrolyte, Li 3 InCl 6 (LIC). The resulting AFI layer concurrently provides ionic conductivity, excellent oxidation stability (>4.8 V), and favorable viscoelasticity, thereby synergistically enhancing the electrochemical, chemical, and mechanical stability of the interface without compromising bulk ion transport. When paired with a single‐crystal ultrahigh‑nickel cathode LiNi 0.94 Co 0.05 Mn 0.01 O 2 (Ni94), the surface‑softened LIC (S‑LIC) enables ASSLBs delivering specific capacities of 223.8 and 209.5 mAh g −1 at 2 C and 4 C, respectively, retaining over 85% of the initial capacity after 2000 cycles at 2 C, and operate stably for more than 9000 cycles at 10 C. Even under an ultrahigh cutoff voltage of 4.8 V, a capacity retention of 81% is achieved after 800 cycles at 2 C. This work provides a broadly applicable and efficient interfacial engineering route for high‑voltage halide‑based ASSLBs.
papers.tldr: A Lewis-acid-induced in situ polymerization of acrylonitrile forms a nanoscale adaptive flexible interphase on Li₃InCl₆ halide electrolyte, enabling high-voltage all-solid-state lithium batteries with high rate capability and long cycling stability.

papers.title: Dynamic Charge Gradients from Interfacial Electron Transfer Enable Self-Powered Gate-Controlled All-Metal-Nanoparticle Neuromorphic Systems
papers.abstract: Abstract Harvesting electricity from ambient moisture represents a transformative approach to power generation, a process traditionally ascribed solely to ion or proton diffusion. Here, we report a moisture-energy-harvesting mechanism that originates from interfacial electron transfer in a ligand-decorated metal nanoparticle film. Partially covering the film creates an asymmetric humidity gradient that triggers unbalanced electron transfer from adsorbed water to the metal nanoparticle core. This establishes a persistent dynamic charge separation and concentration gradient along the film that is sustained by continuous water evaporation from its exposed side, as supported by multiscale simulations. With this mechanism, we demonstrate that the electricity generated by these nanoparticle devices can not only power common microelectronic devices but also be directly integrated with a nanoparticle synaptic transistor to achieve a self-powered gate-controlled all-metal-nanoparticle neuromorphic system.
papers.tldr: A ligand-decorated metal-nanoparticle film harvests ambient moisture via asymmetric interfacial electron transfer, creating a persistent charge gradient that powers microelectronics and enables a self-powered, gate-controlled all-metal-nanoparticle neuromorphic system.

papers.title: Locally Competitive Coordination Electrolyte for High‐Voltage Lithium‐Metal Batteries With Ni‐Rich Cathodes
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium (Li) metal anodes (LMAs) hold great promise to increase the energy density of batteries. This is especially true when using an energy‐dense cathode such as Ni‐rich layered transition metal oxides, but unfortunately, these lead to accelerated capacity loss when combined with LMAs. Ni‐rich cathodes suffer from surface reduction, which can be accelerated in contact with certain electrolyte solvents. This in turn leads to transition metal dissolution and shuttling, which poisons the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) and complicates the anode stabilization. Here, we propose nitrile primary solvent combined with ether co‐solvent, diluent and two borate salts to suppress parasitic reaction. A competition in the ion coordination between solvents surrounded by diluents is achieved. This leads to the anions being preferentially decomposed in the SEI and enhanced reversibility. Using high cathode areal capacity (4.0 mAh cm − 2 ), thin LMAs (N/p = 2.5), lean electrolyte (3 g Ah − 1 ), and high charging voltages (≥4.4 V), we achieve a capacity retention of 80% over 250 cycles. With moderately high loading cathode (3.4 mAh cm − 2 ) but higher upper voltage (4.6 V), the cells retain 87.5% capacity retention over 430 cycles. Finally, we demonstrate Ah‐level anode‐free pouch cells with a 78.7% capacity retention over 100 cycles.
papers.tldr: A nitrile/ether electrolyte with borate salts uses competitive ion coordination to suppress parasitic reactions and stabilize the interphase, enabling high-voltage Ni-rich lithium-metal batteries with high capacity retention and Ah-level anode-free pouch cells.

papers.title: Vertically Graded Dual Salts to Suppress Interfacial Mobile-Ion Accumulation for Stable Perovskite Photovoltaics
papers.abstract: Abstract Suppression of mobile-ion accumulation at the perovskite interface is critical for perovskite photovoltaic (PV) stability. Post-treatment with fluorinated aromatic ammonium salts can suppress ion migration at perovskite interfaces. However, these salts damage underlying three-dimensional (3D) perovskites during device operation, inducing interfacial mobile-ion accumulation. Although these cations form gradient low-dimensional perovskites for enhanced quality of bulk quasi-2D films, constructing an ultrathin gradient structure by post-treatment remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate a preferential spatial arrangement of dual fluorinated ammonium cations at the FA0.95Cs0.05PbI3 perovskite interface, which suppresses the interfacial mobile-ion accumulation. This arrangement includes both long-chain cations on the topmost surface and short-chain cations preferentially in the sub-surface region. This unique surface structure suppresses mobile-ion accumulation at the LD/3D heterostructure. Our n–i–p perovskite PV achieves an efficiency of 26.47% (certified 25.95%). Moreover, the resulting perovskite PVs exhibit an operational stability of 3600 h at 55 °C and a thermal stability of 3500 h at 85 °C.
papers.tldr: A vertically graded dual-fluorinated-ammonium surface treatment suppresses interfacial mobile-ion accumulation in perovskite solar cells, enabling 26.47% efficiency and long-term operational and thermal stability.

papers.title: Multi‐Hydrogen Adsorption as a Dynamic Electronic Gate for Ultrafast Interfacial Charge Transfer
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Reactive materials operate under dynamically evolving adsorption environments, yet how cooperative adsorbates reshape interfacial electronic structure and charge‐transfer kinetics remains poorly understood. Here we show that multi‐hydrogen adsorption can function as a dynamic electronic gate that reprograms interfacial charge‐transfer energetics. Using a sulfur‐rich amorphous CoReS 2+x cocatalyst as a model system, we demonstrate that abundant unsaturated sulfur sites enable cooperative multi‐hydrogen adsorption, which induces spontaneous electron delocalization and generates an electron‐deficient interfacial state. This adsorption‐driven electronic redistribution reverses the thermodynamic directionality of electron injection from CdZnS, converting an originally endothermic process into a spontaneous one. Femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy further reveals that the gated interface accelerates interfacial electron transfer to the ultrafast regime, in agreement with first‐principles calculations. The resulting a‐CoReS 2+x /CdZnS system achieves highly efficient photocatalytic hydrogen evolution from biomass‐derived formic acid with an apparent quantum efficiency of 67.8%. More broadly, these findings establish multi‐adsorbate‐induced electronic gating as a general mechanism for dynamically programming interfacial charge transfer in catalytic and energy‐conversion materials operating under realistic reactive environments.
papers.tldr: Multi-hydrogen adsorption on a sulfur-rich amorphous CoReS₂₊ₓ cocatalyst acts as a dynamic electronic gate that induces interfacial electron delocalization, converts electron injection from CdZnS from endothermic to spontaneous, and enables ultrafast charge transfer for efficient photocatalytic hydrogen evolution from formic acid with 67.8% apparent quantum efficiency.

papers.title: Ordering Mixed-Q Topological Magnetism into Lattice via Moiré Engineering
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract: Abstract Topological magnetic lattices offer a fertile ground for exploring fundamental physics and developing novel spintronic devices. However, current research is predominantly confined to single-Q topologies hosting uniform type of quasiparticle. Here, Q denotes the real-space topological charge of a spin texture, rather than a reciprocal-space ordering wavevector. The realization of exotic mixed-Q states, where distinct topological quasiparticles coassemble into an ordered lattice, remains largely unexplored. Here, we propose a design principle to order disordered mixed-Q topological magnetism into periodic lattice via moiré engineering. By leveraging the synergy between spatially modulated interlayer coupling and intrinsic intralayer magnetic frustration, we demonstrate that moiré potential can effectively regularize skyrmions, antiskyrmions, and magnetic bubbles into a hybrid lattice. Combining first-principles with atomistic spin simulations, we validate this mechanism in twisted bilayer CrGaTe3, identifying it as an exemplary platform for hosting these complex ordered textures. We systematically map the phase evolution as a function of twist angle and biaxial strain, unveiling the critical role of moiré potential in stabilizing mixed-Q lattice. Our findings significantly advance the frontier of topological and moiré spintronics.
papers.tldr: Moiré engineering in twisted bilayer CrGaTe₃ can order mixed-Q topological spin textures—skyrmions, antiskyrmions, and magnetic bubbles—into a stable hybrid periodic lattice by combining spatially modulated interlayer coupling with intrinsic intralayer magnetic frustration.

papers.title: Enhanced room-temperature spin transport in a deuterated molecular single crystal
papers.abstract: Achieving high-efficiency spin transport at room temperature remains a central challenge in spintronics. Molecular single crystals are ideal candidates for addressing this challenge because their highly ordered lattices and uniform transport pathways intrinsically suppress spin scattering and enable long spin lifetimes. However, integrating these intrinsic advantages into practical devices has remained challenging, primarily because molecular single crystals are extremely fragile during device fabrication. Here, we design a molecular single-crystal system with uniform spin-transport pathways and suppressed spin-relaxation channels, resulting in a substantially enhanced room-temperature spin lifetime, as confirmed by both theoretical analysis and experimental characterizations. By applying a damage-free crystal-handling method with an optimized electrode-transfer technique, we fabricate high-quality single-crystal spintronic devices and achieve a spin-transport efficiency of 15.17% at room temperature, nearly twice the previous benchmark (∼8%). This work establishes a generalizable strategy for designing long-spin-lifetime molecular spintronic materials and demonstrates the practical viability of molecular single crystals as a platform for efficient room-temperature spin transport.
papers.tldr: Researchers achieved 15.17% room-temperature spin-transport efficiency—nearly double the previous ~8% benchmark—by designing a deuterated molecular single crystal with uniform spin pathways and suppressed spin relaxation and fabricating it into devices using damage-free crystal handling and optimized electrode transfer.

papers.title: Competing charge and spin instabilities and giant magnetoelastic coupling in CrSb
papers.abstract: Electronic, magnetic, and lattice degrees of freedom are often strongly intertwined in quantum materials, giving rise to competing ordered states and emergent collective phenomena. Understanding how these interactions evolve across symmetry-breaking transitions is essential for identifying new mechanisms of electronic ordering. Here, we show that the antiferromagnet chromium antimonide provides an ideal platform to investigate this interplay and uncover short-range charge-order fluctuations at the M point of the Brillouin zone, q * = ( 1 2 0 ) , persisting well above the Néel temperature, T N . These fluctuations collapse upon entering the magnetically ordered phase, revealing a direct competition between charge and spin order parameters. At T N , the phonon dispersion at q * develops a pronounced Kohn-like anomaly, signaling strong electron-phonon coupling in the vicinity of the magnetic transition. Below T N , exchange striction markedly renormalizes the associated soft phonon mode by ∼6 milli–electron volts, corresponding to the largest spin-phonon coupling reported to date. First-principles calculations show that the relevant phonon branch is unstable at the harmonic level only in the absence of magnetic order, highlighting the remarkable sensitivity of the lattice to magnetic symmetry breaking. The suppression of charge correlations upon magnetic ordering, together with the abrupt reconstruction of the phonon spectrum at T N , demonstrates an exceptional coupling between charge, spin, and lattice degrees of freedom in chromium antimonide. With its chemically simple structure and symmetry-protected altermagnetic state, chromium antimonide emerges as a model system for exploring giant spin-phonon coupling, competing electronic instabilities, and emergent broken symmetries in altermagnetic materials.
papers.tldr: CrSb hosts short-range charge-order fluctuations that compete with antiferromagnetic order and collapse at the Néel temperature, accompanied by a giant Kohn-like phonon anomaly and the largest spin-phonon coupling reported to date, making it a model altermagnet for coupled charge-spin-lattice instabilities.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Guided Precise Electrolyte Engineering Enables Stable Lithium Metal Pouch Cells Exceeding 350 Wh/kg at −40 °C
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract: Abstract High-energy-density lithium metal batteries (LMBs) with wide-temperature adaptability are urgently needed for aerospace and military fields, yet extreme temperature conditions disrupt Li+ transport kinetics and cause failure in solid–electrolyte interphase (SEI) chemistry regulation. To guide molecular selection for wide-temperature electrolyte design, we constructed Electrolyte-65K, a rule-defined library of electrolyte-relevant molecules, and trained D-P Compass using batch-computable molecular descriptors to efficiently predict and rank dipole moment (D) and polarizability (P). Applying the trained models to a literature-derived set of electrolyte molecule candidates, D-P Pareto analysis identified N,N-dimethyltrifluoromethanesulfonamide (DMTMSA) as the candidate at the Pareto knee. The thermally sensitive dipole–dipole interactions between DMTMSA and weakly solvating solvent 1,2-diethoxyethane (DEE) enable a temperature-autoresponsive electrolyte that maintains an anion-dominated solvation structure across a wide temperature range, enabling SEI chemistry engineering regulation from −40 to 60 °C. A 5.8 Ah pouch cell achieves a high energy density of 503.7 Wh kg–1 at 25 °C with a lifespan of 275 cycles and retains 365.5 Wh kg–1 at −40 °C with 99.8% capacity retention over 50 cycles. This work establishes a data-driven molecular screening framework for wide-temperature electrolyte engineering design.
papers.tldr: Using machine-learning-guided molecular screening, researchers identified a DMTMSA/DEE temperature-autoresponsive electrolyte that stabilizes anion-dominated solvation and SEI chemistry, enabling 5.8 Ah lithium-metal pouch cells to retain 365.5 Wh/kg at −40 °C with 99.8% capacity retention over 50 cycles.

papers.title: Atomic Resolution Microscopy Reveals Cluster, Charge Transport, and Diffusion Metrics in Guest:Host Blend Films
papers.abstract: Abstract Quantitatively determining the 3D arrangement of guest molecules in a guest:host emissive layer remains a challenge, particularly for beam-sensitive organic materials. By extracting 3D coordinates from depth-sectioned HAADF–STEM stacks of Ir(ppy)2(acac):TCTA and Ir(ppy)3:TCTA vacuum-deposited guest:host blend films, we enable direct access to molecular-scale morphology in beam-sensitive materials. We find that guest aggregation is significantly stronger than expected from random distributions, with the difference diminishing only at high concentrations. Coupling these morphologies to master equation transport modeling reveals that aggregation alters transport pathways and reduces mobility. Additionally, thermal motion of guest molecules between the image frames provides an estimate of molecular diffusion, linking structural and dynamic behavior.
papers.tldr: Depth-sectioned HAADF–STEM resolves 3D guest-molecule arrangements in beam-sensitive guest:host blend films, revealing stronger-than-random aggregation that alters charge-transport pathways and reduces mobility, while also enabling diffusion estimates from thermal motion.

papers.title: Alleviating the stability-energy density dilemma via electron-donor-mediated orbital symmetry regulation in sodium phosphate cathodes
papers.abstract: Manganese-based sodium super ionic conductor-type cathode materials, leveraging the multielectron redox activity of manganese, represent a promising pathway toward high-energy-density sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). However, the unavoidable generation of Mn 3+ (3d 4 ) species during charge-discharge processes, characterized by asymmetric e g orbital occupancy, triggers octahedral symmetry breaking. This inherent electronic structural instability creates a fundamental contradiction between achieving high energy density and ensuring long cycle life that remains inherently difficult to reconcile. Here, we report an electron-donor–mediated (EDM) mechanism that suppresses Mn 3+ -induced octahedral distortion while preserving high-spin functionality. As electron-donating Fe 3+ and V 3+ are incorporated, Mn 3+ 3d electrons undergo partial delocalization. This electronic redistribution promotes orbital interactions between neighboring transition metal sites through the transition metal-oxygen framework, driving the e g orbitals toward a more symmetric occupation and suppressing octahedral distortion. The EDM-modified cathode demonstrates a high energy density of 492.06 Wh kg −1 . It delivers 178.8 mAh g −1 at 0.1 C and retains 80.2% of its capacity over 2000 cycles at 10 C, paving a novel pathway toward next-generation high-performance SIBs cathode materials.
papers.tldr: Incorporating electron-donating Fe³⁺/V³⁺ into manganese-based sodium phosphate cathodes delocalizes Mn³⁺ 3d electrons and symmetrizes e_g orbital occupancy, suppressing octahedral distortion to simultaneously achieve high energy density and long cycling stability in sodium-ion batteries.

papers.title: Cooperative H2O–CO2 Regulation Reinforces Transport and Interfacial Stability in Deep Eutectic Solvent Electrolytes
papers.abstract: Abstract Deep eutectic solvents (DESs), as representative hydrogen-bonded electrolytes, offer unique solvation environments, high CO2 affinity, and broad opportunities in sustainable fields. However, the high viscosity, sluggish diffusion, and the low-temperature solidification tendency of DESs severely impede their electrochemical performance. This work demonstrates an H2O–CO2 cooperative regulation strategy, in which water effectively lowers the viscosity and preserves fluidity of DESs even at −40 °C, while CO2 stabilizes the hydrated DES interfaces and expands the electrochemical window over a wide temperature range. Such interfaceial stabilization is achieved through a CO2-mediated interfacial molecular mechanism rather than a conventional surface passivation process. Combining electrochemical vibrational spectroscopy, atomic force microscopy, and molecular dynamics simulations, it elucidates that the CO2 lowers the population of electrochemically accessible water at the cathodic interface and reorganizes the local hydrogen-bond network in hydrated DESs, thereby suppressing the hydrogen evolution reaction while preserving the fluidity provided by hydration. This stabilized interface further benefits an increased CO2-to-CO reduction rate by approximately 1 order of magnitude. By resolving the persistent transport-stability trade-off in DES electrolytes, this H2O–CO2 cooperative regulation concept offers molecular insights into nanoscale interfacial hydrogen-bond engineering at viscous electrochemical interfaces and provides a general strategy for CO2 conversion, electrosynthesis, etc.
papers.tldr: A cooperative H2O–CO2 regulation strategy in deep eutectic solvent electrolytes uses water to maintain fluidity down to −40 °C while CO2 stabilizes the interface by reorganizing local hydrogen bonding, suppressing hydrogen evolution, widening the electrochemical window, and boosting CO2-to-CO conversion by about an order of magnitude.

papers.title: Band Structure-Engineered Nanopatterned MoS2/Graphene Heterostructures for Low-Noise Broadband Photodetection
papers.abstract: Abstract Integrating two-dimensional (2D) heterostructures is a promising strategy for high-performance optoelectronics; however, achieving high sensitivity and broadband response while maintaining low-noise operation remains challenging. Here, we report a nanoporous molybdenum disulfide (MoS2)/graphene heterostructure phototransistor fabricated via block copolymer-assisted self-assembly and material-selective etching, which provides a scalable and reproducible approach for large-area fabrication. By employing a precise etching sequence using O2 plasma for graphene and XeF2 gas for MoS2, we successfully realize a periodic nanohole array while preserving interfacial integrity. The resulting nanoporous architecture induces bandgap opening in graphene and introduces a high density of edge states, which enhances trap-assisted photogating in the phototransistor and significantly amplify the photocurrent. As a result, the device exhibits a high photoresponsivity of 24.58 AW–1 and a specific detectivity of 2.33 × 1011 Jones under 405 nm illumination. Notably, the device demonstrates a robust photoresponse in the mid-infrared (MIR) region (≈11 µm), extending beyond the intrinsic bandgap limitation of MoS2 and enabling detection capability spanning from the visible to the MIR regime, compared with previously reported MoS2-based heterostructures operating over narrower spectral ranges. Temperature-dependent measurements confirm that this MIR response originates from genuine optical carrier generation rather than bolometric effects. Furthermore, the nanoporous graphene suppresses excessive dark current via bandgap opening and edge-induced states, enabling improved signal-to-noise characteristics. These results establish nanoporous 2D heterostructures as an effective strategy for ultra-broadband and low-noise photodetection.
papers.tldr: A scalable nanoporous MoS₂/graphene heterostructure phototransistor, fabricated via block-copolymer-assisted self-assembly and selective etching, exploits graphene bandgap opening and edge states to enhance trap-assisted photogating, enabling low-noise broadband photodetection from visible to ~11 µm with high responsivity (24.58 A/W) and detectivity (2.33 × 10¹¹ Jones).

papers.title: Rashba-induced intersubband interference in high-harmonic generation
papers.abstract: High-harmonic spectroscopy is exquisitely sensitive to the electronic structure and dynamics of quantum materials, yet quantum interference between spin-orbit-split bands has remained experimentally elusive. We observe this interference between Rashba-split bands in bismuth tellurium iodide (BiTeI) driven by strong mid-infrared laser fields. The sixth harmonic exhibits intensity-scaling kinks and an M-shaped ellipticity dependence. Theoretical simulations attribute these features to spin-orbit–mediated multichannel quantum interference, which arises from Landau-Zener-Stückelberg–type intersubband tunneling between Rashba-split bands. The suppression of harmonic yield under linearly polarized pulses arises from destructive interference among electron-hole recombination pathways, whereas increasing ellipticity modifies their relative phase and induces a distinct spectral redshift. These results establish high-harmonic spectroscopy as a probe of spin-textured band dynamics and ultrafast spin-polarized currents.
papers.tldr: Using high-harmonic spectroscopy in BiTeI, researchers observe Rashba-split-band quantum interference mediated by spin-orbit-coupled intersubband tunneling, enabling ultrafast probes of spin-textured band dynamics.

papers.title: Dynamic Site Heterogeneity in Nanoparticle Catalysis from Hierarchical Machine Learning
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract: Abstract Identifying the activity of all individual surface sites on catalytic nanoparticles is challenging but critical for heterogeneous catalysts, especially for understanding site heterogeneity. Here, we developed a hierarchical machine learning approach that links the atomic local environment to both energy and reaction barrier predictions with similar computational costs, opening the feasibility of extensive catalytic reactivity exploration on nanoparticle catalysts. Applying the methodology to propane dehydrogenation at a reaction temperature of 973 K on Pt nanoparticles up to a size of 5 nm revealed a highly dynamic and heterogeneous activity with a wide distribution of propane C–H cleavage barriers (0.5–1.3 eV) and rare highly active or inactive sites. Conventional global optimization methods underestimate the catalytic activity, even by considering a large set of metastable structures. Instead, accurate activity and size effect trend emerge by using ensemble-averaged molecular dynamics trajectories, emphasizing the dynamic nature of site activity and heterogeneity. Notably, classical polyhedral models, like those obtained from a Wulff construction, can predict correct trends for larger nanoparticles but do so through error cancellation between missing dynamics and overestimating probabilities of metastable sites. Furthermore, our simulations reveal a fast barrier fluctuation at the reaction temperature for a given surface Pt atom within 100 ps trajectories with a barrier shift by up to 0.8 eV, indicating that individual atoms can switch between active and inactive states on a picosecond time scale. This work provides a feasible approach to shift the views of catalysts from a combination of static active sites to highly heterogeneous and fast dynamically evolving sites.
papers.tldr: A hierarchical machine-learning approach reveals that Pt nanoparticle catalytic sites are highly dynamic and heterogeneous, with individual surface atoms switching activity on picosecond timescales, so ensemble-averaged molecular dynamics is needed to predict accurate activity and size trends.

papers.title: Solvent Dipole Engineering Enables Large Quantum Dot Processing for Scalable Short-Wave Infrared Optoelectronics
papers.abstract: Abstract Semiconducting quantum dots (QDs) are key building blocks for optoelectronics, with tunable properties that depend on their size, shape, and surface chemistry. Large lead sulfide (PbS) QDs are particularly attractive for short-wave infrared (SWIR) optoelectronics, yet their processability is hindered by neutral facets, which compromise colloidal stability during liquid-phase ligand exchange and often lead to a collapse of the colloidal ink prior to processing. Herein, we demonstrate that solvent dipole engineering is an effective route for the scalable processing of large PbS QDs, eliminating the need for a layer-by-layer ligand exchange. The approach is utilized to fabricate SWIR-active photovoltaic diodes and photodetectors responsive over a broad spectral range, paving the way for their scalable production and commercialization.
papers.tldr: Solvent dipole engineering enables scalable processing of large PbS quantum dots without layer-by-layer ligand exchange, allowing fabrication of short-wave infrared photovoltaic diodes and photodetectors.

papers.title: Electric field–controlled spin transport in a topological insulator interfaced with a ferroelectric antiferromagnet
papers.abstract: Topological insulators have been explored extensively for spin-charge interconversion via magnetic interfaces, yet the true response of their spin-charge conversion, particularly in the absence of an external magnetic field, remains to be studied. Here, we report electric field control of spin-charge conversion in the topological insulator Bi 2 Te 3 with the antiferromagnetic multiferroic BiFeO 3 , using a nonlocal spin transport device. A systematic thickness dependence of the spin transport across the interface between Bi 2 Te 3 and BiFeO 3 reveals a signature of topological surface-state–dominated spin transport in the bilayer system. The spin-charge conversion remains robust for thicknesses above 10 nanometers but falls rapidly with reducing thickness and vanishes at 5 nanometers. This is consistent with hybridization-induced emergence of a trivial insulating phase, which is supported by the coherency factor estimated from the magnetoconductance of Bi 2 Te 3 . These results establish that spin-momentum–locked surface states dominate interfacial spin transport in the decoupled regime. Beyond presenting efficient spin-charge interconversion at an entirely insulating magnetic interface, this work also highlights sputter-deposited Bi 2 Te 3 as a high-quality and scalable platform for integrating quantum materials onto the devices. The nonlocal spin transport approach presented here provides a simple and unprecedented direct evidence of spin-charge conversion and opens an efficient and practical pathway toward designing energy-efficient spin-based devices.
papers.tldr: Electric-field control of spin-charge conversion in a Bi₂Te₃/BiFeO₃ topological-insulator/ferroelectric-antiferromagnet interface is shown by nonlocal spin transport to be dominated by topological surface states above 10 nm and suppressed at 5 nm due to hybridization-induced trivial insulation, enabling scalable, energy-efficient spin devices.

papers.title: Dopant-Enhanced Polarization in ReS2 Field-Effect Transistor
papers.abstract: Abstract Optical polarization provides an additional degree of freedom for photonic communication, yet its electrical readout requires photodetectors with strong in-plane anisotropy. Here we identify Pt through first-principles screening as a candidate for enhancing the in-plane anisotropy of ReS2. Calculations for the proposed S-site substitution model predict directional orbital hybridization and anisotropic band reconstruction. ReS2 field-effect transistors with 0.93 at. % Pt exhibit polarization-dependent current anisotropic ratios up to 16, compared with 1.45 for pristine devices. Pt incorporation also reduces the contact resistance to 0.85 kΩ·μm, accompanied by lower thermionic and tunneling barriers. Device-calibrated proof-of-concept simulations demonstrate polarization-dependent image decoding, with the peak signal-to-noise ratio increasing from 12.2 to 37.3 dB as the number of states per RGB channel increases from 2 to 10. These findings provide a route toward compact and integrated polarization-sensitive optoelectronic devices.
papers.tldr: Platinum doping of ReS₂ field-effect transistors enhances in-plane anisotropy and polarization-dependent current ratios (up to 16 vs. 1.45), lowers contact resistance, and enables compact polarization-sensitive optoelectronic image decoding.

papers.title: Automatic on-chip separation of partially coherent light into its mutually incoherent components
papers.abstract: Abstract While partial coherence often degrades interference and information transfer, its correlations can be engineered to enhance imaging and optical information processing. However, approaches based on tomography and numerical reconstruction do not physically separate unknown fields into their coherence modes—that is, their orthogonal and mutually incoherent components. Here we demonstrate the separation of partially coherent light into coherence modes. We use variational processing in layered self-configuring interferometers on a silicon photonic circuit. This process finds the eigenvectors and eigenvalues of the coherency matrix, characterizing the state while leaving it intact and separated after optimization. We show that spatially orthogonal, mutually incoherent beams can be routed to separate outputs even when their intensity profiles overlap. Our experiment separates the two strongest coherence modes from a nine-input sampling of overlapping fields from two independent lasers; operation beyond two modes is verified in a rank-3 experiment. The number of physical components scales linearly with the rank r of the coherency matrix, through r in situ gradient-based optimizations enabled by electronic drive-frequency multiplexing of the phase shifters. We benchmark performance against an on-chip mixture-based tomographic method. These results establish a scalable framework for programmable coherence analysis and control.
papers.tldr: Researchers demonstrate an on-chip silicon photonic interferometer that automatically and physically separates partially coherent light into its mutually incoherent coherence modes, scaling linearly with coherency-matrix rank and outperforming mixture-based tomography.
